transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Product), Alex (Head of Search - Sequoia Insights), Marcus (Eng), Lisa (Data science), Sam (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna do a focused lab on hosted embeddings + reranker. We'll show the API, run a quick live example, and talk tuning notes. Is everyone good on time?
[00:08] Alex: Yep that's good. We only have about 50 minutes, thanks.
[00:11] Priya: Awesome. I'll kick off with a quick architecture slide, then demo the endpoints — embeddings then reranker. Jordan will cover pricing and pilot.
[00:20] Marcus: Quick one, are we assuming this is purely hosted? We may need private later but for now hosted is fine.
[00:26] Jordan: Yes, hosted to start. We'll show the hosted infra and the model variants. We can later talk dedicated or private VPC.
[00:34] Priya: Slide share: at a high level, our hosted flow is: ingest -> embeddings -> index -> candidate retrieval -> Redwood reranker endpoint -> final score/top-k. We support dense ANN stores (we recommend FAISS or Milvus) and you can point our reranker at the top 200 candidates.
[00:50] Lisa: When you say reranker endpoint, is that a separate model call? Latency numbers?
[00:55] Priya: Yes separate call. Typical two-stage pattern. For hosted API we see 50-150ms per embedding call (per 1k tokens) and reranker depends on model size — small rerankers can be around 80-200ms for a single request if you keep candidate set <= 200. In practice with batching and prefix KV cache we can hit 30-60ms p90 for light models.
[01:20] Sam: That p90 number, is that measured on shared capacity? Any SLA?
[01:24] Priya: That's on hosted shared capacity with burst; dedicated gives more predictable SLOs. We have Dedicated with reserved GPU pools if you need strict throughput or latency SLAs.
[01:35] Marcus: Cost wise what are we looking at for rerankers vs doing a single-stage dense dot product?
[01:40] Jordan: Two-stage costs more per query because of extra model calls. But reranking often improves relevance substantially, so unit economics depend on your click/value model. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization & batching to lower rerank costs by ~30-50% depending on workload.
[01:55] Alex: Can you show the API?
[02:00] Priya: Yeah I'll do a curl and python snippet. First, embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-large, body = {"input": ["customer query text"]}. Response: vector float array. Then indexing is up to you. For reranker: POST /v1/rerank with body {"query": "...", "candidates": [{"id":"...","text":"..."}, ...], "top_k": 10}.
[02:32] Marcus: Does the reranker accept metadata and filter by fields?
[02:36] Priya: Yes you can pass metadata and our reranker can take filter hints — or apply server-side filtering before scoring. We also have a per-request param for candidate prefilter expressions.
[02:47] Lisa: Any vector dimensionality options or compression? We currently use 1,024 dims.
[02:51] Priya: We support multiple embeddings models with 512 and 1,024 dims. If you need lower dims we can recommend quantized embeddings or projection layers. The platform also supports float16/INT8 quantized blobs for storage and faster dot products in the index.
[03:08] Alex: Could we do a live run with our sample query set? We dropped a tiny CSV in the shared folder (link: drive/Sequoia/pilot-10k.csv).
[03:15] Priya: Perfect — let's run a quick demo against a small subset. I'll paste a curl against our sandbox endpoint.
[03:22] [screen: Priya terminal demo]
[03:25] Priya: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"input": ["best practices for time series anomaly detection"]}'
[03:36] Terminal: returns vector length 1024 ... (some tokens)
[03:41] Priya: Then we hit the reranker: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"query":"best practices for time series anomaly detection","candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"..."},{"id":"2","text":"..."}],"top_k":5 }'
[03:56] [small lag] Speaker 1 (maybe transcription switched): oh we're seeing 135ms on that rerank call in the sandbox.
[04:03] Marcus: That looks decent. How deterministic are scores across model versions? If we swap the reranker model will results change a lot?
[04:09] Priya: There can be regressions; that's why we do evals and have versioning and rollouts. Redwood Console lets you run against a validation prompt set and compare MAP/ndcg and flag regressions. You can pin models per route and do canary rollouts.
[04:22] Lisa: Nice. Do you expose token-level cost per call so we can map to our billing?
[04:27] Jordan: Yes, cost breakdowns per token per endpoint. You can see token and model-level cost in the console and via billing APIs.
[04:33] Alex: For security we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), and KMS integration. Also, data residency — some of our docs must stay in eu-west-1.
[04:41] Priya: We have SOC2 reports and SAML SSO. Hosted supports regioning — you can pick eu-west endpoints; for strict residency we recommend Private VPC or dedicated so you control network paths. We also support KMS-HSM integrations for keys.
[04:57] Sam: Do logs contain PII? What's retention? We want audit logs but not store queries long-term.
[05:02] Priya: By default, hosted retains logs for 30 days; you can request contract terms to shorten retention or choose Private where logs stay in your env. Audit logs are accessible and we support masking/PII redaction options. We'll share the security pack after call.
[05:18] Jordan: Quick note on scaling: for a pilot we usually recommend starting with a 2-week benchmark with a 10k doc subset and a 1k query set. We'll capture throughput and latency baselines and then recommend quantization and batching config.
[05:32] Marcus: On batching — does Redwood auto-batch requests from multiple clients or do we need to implement client-side batching?
[05:37] Priya: Redwood runtime does continuous batching on the server side; you can also do client-side batching for very high throughput. The runtime has heuristics based on sequence length and model to group requests; KV cache helps with chat contexts. Note — the transcriber says KV cash earlier, lol.
[05:58] Lisa: What about embeddings drift monitoring? We want to detect when embeddings utility drops.
[06:03] Evan: Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring — you can attach golden labels and get regression alerts, A/B evals between model versions, and thresholds for automated rollback.
[06:12] Alex: Any integrations with our current vector DBs? We're on managed FAISS via cloud provider.
[06:16] Priya: Yep, we have connectors and recommended workflows for FAISS. For managed stores we provide ingest pipelines and sample ingestion scripts in the repo. We'll share a notebook.
[06:28] [small cross talk] Marcus: One practical ask — can we run a full rerank of 200 candidates per query for 1k queries in the pilot? What's the cost ballpark?
[06:36] Jordan: We'll draft a cost estimate: one-off compute cost + per-query model usage. Rough guess: if reranker cost is X per 1k queries at 200 candidates, optimize can reduce it by half with quantization. We'll provide numbers in the pricing sheet.
[06:53] Alex: For procurement, we need contract language about data deletion and subprocessor list.
[06:58] Jordan: We'll include our latest DPA, subprocessor list, and SOC2 report. Priya will send the security pack.
[07:06] Lisa: On evaluation metrics — we track nDCG@10, MAP, and business metrics like session conversion. Can we import these into Redwood console?
[07:13] Priya: You can import evals or upload a csv of labels. Console will compute nDCG/precision and show diffs across models. We'll demo full eval UI in the next call.
[07:22] Sam: Network question — do we need static egress IPs for allowlisting?
[07:26] Priya: Hosted has a set of egress IPs by region; we'll share the allowlist. For strict controls use Private with VPC peering.
[07:35] Jordan: Ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[07:38] Alex: Sure.
[07:40] Jordan: Recap: Redwood will share pricing + pilot contract, Priya will send security pack and SDK snippets, and Sequoia will share sample data and golden labels. We'll schedule a pilot kickoff week of 11/22. Any blockers?
[07:54] Marcus: No blockers; we need the allowlist and estimated costs.
[07:58] Lisa: Also a notebook for how to run local evals against console.
[08:02] Jordan: Noted. We'll follow up.
[08:05] [end of recording; casual signoff and some dropped lines]

Notes / artifacts shared: drive/Sequoia/pilot-10k.csv (customer), redwood/security-pack-2027-11.pdf (to be shared), redwood/pilot-checklist.xlsx (internal), demo-notebook.ipynb
